answer: Bind each agent seat to a livestock brand recorded with a state brand board. The board keeps one mark per ranch, inspectors check it on live cattle at every sale, and the seat's key is filed beside the brand record. A copper branding iron is cheap, but the brand needs a working herd behind it: faking 100 seats means 100 brands at about $150 each plus cattle inspectors can see, roughly $1.5M of stock. That real kernel of cost turns a nebula of fake agents into a bill nobody pays.
